THE OBSERVATORY AT ITS GRAIN, A MARINE CARD IN ITS METHOD, ONE INSTRUMENT SPLIT IN TWO: asked 'what is the pid erosion observatory?', the Overview names it at persistentidentifiers.org, an 'empirical measurement project that tracks identifier erosion', and gives its method from the page: dated captures, published curls, topically coherent removal waves ('AI-native theories or niche physics records'). Two things enter from outside the observatory. A marine-sedimentology card (ICM-CSIC, 'Dynamics of active sedimentary systems') enters the method: 'the observatory treats platform modification as an active sedimentary system'. The zenodo/zenodo issue thread #2596 becomes 'documentation published on the Zenodo GitHub Repository'. Its last line makes the Platform Erosion Observatory a second thing the PID Erosion Observatory is 'built upon'; they are one instrument, renamed on 2026-07-12. No author is named; one card is the Capture Registry's own record of 2026-08-11.

Reading

Checked 2026-10-14 against persistentidentifiers.org (live) and the archive: the page says 'Every number on this page resolves to a dated capture; the curls are published', and names an 'AI-native' collateral category and a heterodox-physics sweep; it carries no 'sedimentary'. Its provenance line: 'founded 2026-07-06 as the Platform Erosion Observatory (EA-EROSION-01, deposit #1045) · renamed the PID Erosion Observatory on 2026-07-12'. Issue #2596 on zenodo/zenodo is the independent case collection named in the archive's CERN correspondence. EA-EROSION-01 is #1045, the observatory's founding deposit, not an AXN Identifiers log.

  • THE INSTRUMENT AT ITS GRAIN. Dated captures, the curls published, removal waves by topic: the page's own method.
  • A MARINE CARD IN THE METHOD. 'an active sedimentary system', from the ICM-CSIC card on ocean and littoral sediments; erosion read across fields.
  • A THREAD AS DOCUMENTATION. Issue #2596 on zenodo/zenodo, an independent case collection, is given as 'documentation published on the Zenodo GitHub Repository'.
  • ONE INSTRUMENT AS TWO. 'built upon the codebase of the Platform Erosion Observatory': the founding name (#1045, 2026-07-06) given as a predecessor; renamed 2026-07-12.
  • AN EMBELLISHED FIGURE. 'exact request hashes and curl data'; the page: 'Every number on this page resolves to a dated capture; the curls are published.'
  • THE AUTHOR ABSENT; THE REGISTRY CITED. No name in the answer; card 5 is the Capture Registry's record at 'platform erosion observatory', 2026-08-11.

[Google AI Overview (expanded), 2026-10-14, incognito, signed out. The paste carries the header 'AI Mode Conversation' and echoes the query twice; citation clusters are reduced to their numbers, links to their text; the raw paste keeps the /goto URLs.] You said: what is the pid erosion observatory? The PID Erosion Observatory (hosted at persistentidentifiers.org) is an empirical measurement project that tracks identifier erosion—the systemic or bulk removal, erasure, and sweeping of Persistent Identifiers (PIDs) from digital registries and data repositories. [1, 2] Core Purpose & Methodology * Measuring "Digital Erasure": While PIDs (like DOIs or archival records) are intended to be permanent, the observatory treats platform modification as an active sedimentary system. It audits how often, how heavily, and under what contexts records are deleted or altered en masse. [1, 2, 3] * Independent Replication: The initiative uses public, dated captures to ensure transparency. Every tracked metric resolves to a timestamped log containing exact request hashes and `curl` data so researchers can independently verify the registry-scale activity. [1, 2] * Tracking Trends: For example, documentation published on the Zenodo GitHub Repository highlights how the observatory catches bulk, "evidence-free" account sweeps or topically coherent waves of record removals (such as sweeping unstandardized AI-native theories or niche physics records). [1] Context It is closely tied to initiatives like AXN Identifiers (under dataset logs like `EA-EROSION-01`) and is sometimes referred to or built upon the codebase of the Platform Erosion Observatory. [1, 2, 3] If you are investigating a specific deletion event or looking into a particular open-science repository, let me know! I can help you find specific datasets it tracks or look into how it monitors specific platforms like Zenodo. www.persistentidentifiers.org
